plan.topic: Looking at the medicine in your tirzepatide pen before the shot: what the Instructions for Use say it should look like (colour, clarity, particles), and what to do if it doesn't
plan.angle: Name the source: 'Zepbound single-dose pen IFU (US)'. If the Mounjaro pen IFU says the same thing at its own working URL, add it as 'Mounjaro pen: same check, see its own IFU'. By 6 s, paraphrase or quote the label: the medicine should be clear and colourless to slightly yellow, and don't use it if you see particles or discolouration. Add 'cloudy' and 'frozen' only if the IFU URL loads and prints them. Scope card: 'US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets; check the one in your box.' Untagged line: 'Not sure? Don't use it. Ask your pharmacist or call the number in your IFU.' Drop the injection-site stat card. Keep the closing as planned, with no subscribe or link line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide Pen: What Should the Medicine Look Like? #shorts
plan.why: Visible pen 'Is this normal?' Shorts are our proven 08:00 winners (pen blood 111, injection site 254 and 202). This moment hasn't been covered yet, and the evidence is low-risk and IFU-only. | fact-check: Low risk and useful. I checked the Zepbound label on uspl.lilly.com, which says the medicine is 'clear and colorless to slightly yellow' and 'Do not use ZEPBOUND if particulate matter or discoloration is seen.' 'Cloudy' and 'frozen' are allowed only if the pen IFU's own URL loads and prints them. Air bubbles go in only if that IFU mentions them. 'Tirzepatide pen' is ambiguous: Mounjaro and Zepbound have separate US single-dose pen IFUs, so the Short must name which IFU it is quoting. The optional injection-site stat card (6–8% vs about 2%) has nothing to do with what the medicine looks like, and a viewer could read it as cloudy medicine causing reactions. Drop it.

That split-second glance at your pen before a shot? Here's exactly what to look for.

Two things the US Zepbound label says to check every time:

💧 Color: should be clear and colorless to slightly yellow. A faint yellow tint still fits the label.

🔍 Particles: don't use it if you see particles or discoloration.

Your pen or vial also comes with its own Instructions for Use, so check the one in your box.

Not sure what you're seeing? Don't use it yet. Call your pharmacist or prescriber first.

factcheck.summary: I checked every claim in the script against the US Zepbound label (revised 8/2026), and the script is accurate and safe. Section 2.4 says the medicine "should appear clear and colorless to slightly yellow. Do not use ZEPBOUND if particulate matter or discoloration is seen." That backs s2, s3 and s4. The same section supports s5's point that each presentation (single-dose pen, vial, KwikPen) has its own Instructions for Use. The Mounjaro label (Section 2.2, revised 8/2026) has the same inspection wording, so calling it a "tirzepatide pen" in s1 is supported for the US. The hook pays off, there are no dosing or don't-stop problems, and the Short ending follows the 11-17 format. Two minor fixes: add the Mounjaro label as a source, since the target keyword names Mounjaro, and make the s6 help line rely only on what we've verified. Neither needs a full re-check.
